messages:
alex_support: FYI customer (AcmePayments) opened an escalation — streaming sessions drop under bursty load. Python iterator yields a partial chunk, then stops. Repro on our infra with 200 concurrent clients.

nina_support: Can you paste a minimal repro and the environment (python, sdk version, server region)?

alex_support: Repro summary: 200 parallel clients, token refresh every 30s, python 3.11, SDK v0.14.2. Minimal loop: `for token in client.stream(...): process(token)` We see iterator return a short token then complete unexpectedly. Logs (raw SSE lines captured on client):
```
event: message
data: {"type":"chunk","text":"Payment confirmed: 1"}


event: heartbeat
data: {}


event: message
data: {"type":"chunk","text":"23"}


event: message
data:


event: eof
data: {"final":true}

```
Notice the empty `data:` line before the `eof`. The python iterator yields "23" then an empty string and stops (no final frame).

ryan_p_sdk: Hmm looks like a framing/interleaving issue when heartbeat or other control events arrive while we're assembling a chunk. We landed a non-blocking heartbeat handler in 0.14.0 to reduce latency — could be an async race that causes the SSE parser to emit an empty `data` event. Do you have raw server request ids?

alex_support: Pasted one request id in headers: `x-rw-req-id: rw-req-8f7a3` and session id `sess-42bf`. Happened across eu-west and us-east.

devon_eng: We started multiplexing session streams on sockets in the runtime patch (Q4) to increase density. If the parser treats `\n\n` sequences incorrectly when multiple event types are queued, the client-side iterator might see an empty payload. That would explain the partial yield then close.

qa_bot: Suggest testing with SDK v0.13.6 (pre-heartbeat change) — quick canary to check regression.

nina_support: Ran quick test: pinned to v0.13.6 and stress repro completed with no empty yields. So it's likely a regression introduced in >=0.14.0. Customer still on 0.14.2.

ryan_p_sdk: Plan: add guard in the SSE parser to ignore events where `data` is empty or purely whitespace. Also ensure iterator only yields non-empty text chunks and only terminates on explicit `eof`/close. I'll prepare a patch and a canary build.

alex_support: Customer also flagged potential billing duplication — when final frames are duplicated we could bill twice for the same token. Can infra confirm server-side dedupe?

devon_eng: We should not rely solely on client dedupe. I'll add a server-side idempotency check keyed by `x-rw-req-id` + event-id for final frames and emit metric `streaming_duplicate_final_frame_count`. Opening infra ticket now.

ryan_p_sdk: Quick proposed hotfix (for SDK):
```py
# in sse_parser.py
if not data_str.strip():
    # ignore empty data events introduced by interleaved control events
    continue
# existing handling
yield parsed_chunk
```
I'll also add unit tests that simulate heartbeat interleaving and a stress CI job.

nina_support: Can you post the canary build and test plan here so we can coordinate with the customer? They want timeline and whether a rollback to 0.13.6 is safe temporarily.

ryan_p_sdk: Canary build URL: https://internal-ci.redwood/artefacts/sdk/0.14.3-canary1 — includes parser guard + dedupe tests. Test plan: 1) 2k parallel clients for 10m, 2) token rotation every 15-30s, 3) validate no empty yields and final frame arrives once.

ops-bot: ticket created: INFRA-5843 (server-side dedupe) — assigned to devon_eng.

devon_eng: I'll sync with infra and prioritize dedupe. If canary passes we can push SDK patch to customers and recommend rolling back if they prefer immediate mitigation. :thumbsup:

alex_support: Thanks — I'll share canary with AcmePayments and ask them to test this afternoon. Will update here with their feedback. :eyes:
